Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Sharma 1982:127 (Table 10.0, sec. 10.1.1). Value 1 confirmed under the existential convention (ergative present on at least one form of the person). NUMBER SPLIT: the 1SG is syncretic (Nom = Ag = ge/gye), so the singular shows no overt ergative; but the dual and plural distinguish ergative from nominative (Nom neku/nere vs. Ag nekui/neci). The 1 reflects the dual/plural. Parallel to noct1238 (Hakhun) GB409_2, where 1SG is nominative-accusative but 1PL is ergative.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Sharma 1982:128 (sec. 10.1.2). Value 1 confirmed. No number split: agentive distinct from nominative in all three numbers (Nom kae:/keku/kere vs. Ag kai/kekui/keci). Precise page is 128, not 127.

curated_comment: Verified against Sharma 1982:128 (sec. 10.1.3). Value 1 confirmed. No number split: agentive distinct from nominative in all three numbers (Nom do/doku/dore vs. Ag doi/dokui/doci). Precise page is 128, not 127.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Verified against Sharma 1982:114-118 (sec. 9.4 paradigms; sec. 9.5.3 alignment). Value 1 confirmed. Nouns distinguish nominative (zero in sg) from agentive (katui, mizi, ghwane). Sec. 9.5.3: A = agentive, P = nominative; sec. 9.5.1: S = nominative. S = P = nominative (absolutive), A = agentive (ergative). Unconditioned by TAM (sec. 9.5.4).
